purpose: Every strategy in this project sizes positions by volatility estimated from closing prices alone, discarding the open, high and low that are already on disk. Range-based estimators use the whole bar and are several times more statistically efficient. Better sizing is a free improvement if it holds, and this measures whether it does.
plain_statement: We only ever looked at where each day ended. Each day also has a start, a high and a low. This asks whether using the whole day makes the portfolio better.
data_correctness_note: The vintage stores raw open/high/low/close alongside a split- and dividend-adjusted close. The adjustment factor ranges from 0.55 to 1.00 on SPY alone, so raw bars must be scaled by adjusted_close/close before any range estimator touches them. Mixing an adjusted close with unadjusted highs and lows would corrupt every estimate silently.

estimators.name: yang_zhang
estimators.note: the only one of these that handles overnight gaps

declared_before_running.applied_to: the Step 201 cross-asset trend sleeve, changing only the volatility input to its inverse-volatility sizing; the signal, universe, rebalance, delay and costs are untouched
declared_before_running.secondary_measurement: estimator efficiency, as the standard deviation of each estimator's own rolling estimate; a more efficient estimator produces a steadier reading of the same underlying volatility

hypotheses: Range estimators should be steadier than close-to-close on the same data, which is a property of the estimator and should appear regardless of whether returns improve.
Steadier sizing should mean less unnecessary rebalancing, so turnover should fall.
Any Sharpe improvement is expected to be small. A large one would be suspicious rather than encouraging.
not_claimed: This changes sizing only. It cannot create a signal that was not already there.
No estimator is selected. All five are reported.
